title: Starting my journey with AI and Unity3D. can someone help?
author: ziadd_hh
selftext:
since unity now has offical plugins for ClaudeCode and Codex, I want to know which is better in terms of costs and weekly limits.

GPT 6 Astra and Fable are expensive. and im just going to buy a plus/pro plan (the 20$ one). my game assets, UI and scenes are already finished.

 i just need the AI model to functiom the UI, generate the save and in-game currency system, create a system for "buy cars and upgrades". and other menu settings and systems like these.

and for the gameplay scenes: make it generate the controllers and features like police chase and other management stuff.

as i said the assets and scenes are ready i just need the codes and physics from AI.

so which AI will be able to handle this without interruption because of weekly limits? Opus or GPT 6 Sol are efficient in this situation? or better to choose older models?

ill be grateful for anyone's opinion, thank you.

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body:
Opus is more efficient right now. We never know how long that will last. A few weeks ago Astra was the more efficient one as it nailed tasks on the first go and you got more bang for your buck. But now Astra has been dumbed down so much getting a reasonable task completion takes 10-20% of a x20 plan, even when dispatching Luna subagents.

So, take that for what you will.

replies.author: ziadd_hh
replies.body: how does plans actually compare? i saw someone on youtube said if a model used 20% week limit of a pro 5x thats like 100% week limit of a plus plan. thats for ChatGPT. is this true? and does it weekly limits for separate models? like weekly limit for GPT5 and another weekly limit for GPT6 or is this false?

replies.author: CycleMother2006
replies.body:
1x = Standard Plan / amount  
Max 5x = 5 standard plans worth of usage  
Max 20x = 20 standard plans (for GPT).  For Claude there is never a point in going above 5x because the 20x only increases your 5 hour window amount by 4x and doesn't give you any more weekly usage, so you can basically use an entire week's worth of allowance in a single sitting with that one.

And yes you can probably burn through a week's worth of GPT or Claude in one sitting on the $20 Pro plan. It doesn't go nearly as far as it used to, though it does depend heavily on your actual use case. Smaller projects require a lot less context which is why you can see people one-shot a slice of something from scratch and it only uses like 20% of their weekly.

comments.author: shuozhe
comments.body: Muse spark 1.3 contributor. Free on OpenCode currently, but meta trains on your code. 1.4 should be there also soon. There will be always a preview/contributor model that is free in the near future.

comments.author: M4xs0n
comments.body:
Everyone will recommend you using Opus 5.5 now. A few weeks ago everyone would say use GPT-6 instead of Claude. My take: work with the one that you are familar with or already pay for. There isn’t a right or wrong, especially when you are starting out. Once you have a working workflow, you can decide if you wanna try out another one.

For Unity, there is also the AI Assistant Bezi. It’s awesome and uses multiple LLMs in the background and it’s own Credit System.

replies.author: ziadd_hh
replies.body: im more familiar with ChatGPT, its my main Ai that i use generally. but now all i care about is the weekly limits and costing rather than which one. both are good AI models

replies.author: M4xs0n
replies.body: If you work on your own game you should be ready to Upgrade your current plan tbh

comments.author: UncleJoesLandscaping
comments.body:
Do you guys connect the AI model straight to Unity or to your IDE? I have mostly been using the assistants built into Rider which is connected to Unity,
 but I am thinking of changing my workflow.

comments.body: I use Codex with Unity plugin, then powershell (Unity CLI). Everything is pretty straightforward...

replies.author: ziadd_hh
replies.body: how much does the weekly limit last with you? and which plan are you on?

replies.author: Youriberg
replies.body: I have ChatGPT Plus, with Astra and Sol, the limit goes away kinda quick, but as most of things I require don't need too much intelligence, I use Luna and it goes away very very slowly (also it makes things very slowly, but I have time so...). I have free credits from Azure so I'll see if I can use the API if I really need to, but I never used Codex/ChatGPT outside from browser until today, so I'm not sure about all the features it really has.

comments.body: Enjoys the learning curve man, use AI as a teacher.
